prompt: A clock moves at $0.80c$ relative to the Earth. The clock records a time interval of $30\ \text{s}$. What time interval does an observer on the Earth measure for the same two events?
markscheme: **C.** $\gamma = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - 0.80^2}} = \tfrac{1}{0.60} = \tfrac{5}{3}$. The clock measures proper time, so $\Delta t = \gamma \Delta t_0 = \tfrac{5}{3} \times 30 = 50\ \text{s}$.
